Vibe coding accepts whatever the agent produces. Agentic engineering writes the
requirements, the constraints and the checks first, then commissions the agent
to build inside them. This project works out what that means for
pharmacometrics and data analysis work, where the deliverable is usually an
argument supported by numbers rather than a running service.

Two questions drive it. How is the initial specification written, and who
writes it. Everything else follows from those.

The guide is evergreen: it is revised as the practice changes rather than
finished. It is also the template that new projects in this repository start
from.

## Documents

- [Working specification](specification.qmd). What is already in place here,
  how to write the initial spec, how the work divides between Andy and the
  agent, and what a new project starts with.
- [References](references.qmd). The sources this draws on, and a marker on
  each recording whether the claim drawn from it has been checked against the
  source.
- `acop_abstract_2027_idea.md`. A draft idea for an ACoP 2027 abstract on the
  pharmacometrics case: the five stages of an analysis, who reviews what, and
  what changes once an agent does the hands-on work. Not linked, because the
  site renders `.qmd` only and this one stays a working file in the
  repository.

## Related reading

[Context Engineering for AI-Assisted Pharmacometrics: A Practical Tutorial](https://ascpt.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/psp4.70317)
(Pritchard-Bell et al., 2026) describes task definitions that give an agent the
domain rules, verification criteria and examples it needs at each step. Tasks
start with fresh context and pass results through workspace files.

My reservation is the covariate-selection rule: the tutorial specifies an
objective function value decrease of ΔOFV > 3.84 for inclusion and uses forward
selection and backward elimination. I tend to prefer a full covariate model,
with scientifically motivated covariates specified together, because stepwise
selection can overfit noise. I would want the task definition to reflect that
choice before asking an agent to develop the covariate model.
